angle: The American Farm Bureau's 41st annual survey (Nov. 18, 2026): a classic Thanksgiving dinner for 10 costs $58.63, up 6%, the first rise since the 2022 record of $64.05. The turkey leads: $23.68 for 16 lb, up 10%. Timed for Thanksgiving week.
paragraphs: This year, a classic Thanksgiving dinner for ten costs {fifty-eight dollars and sixty-three cents|$58.63}.
That's about {five eighty-six|$5.86} a person, and {six percent|6%} more than last year.
The biggest jump is the turkey. A sixteen-pound bird costs {twenty-three sixty-eight|$23.68}, up {ten percent|10%}.
Cranberries are up almost {nine percent|9%}. A gallon of milk, up {eight point six|8.6} percent.
A few things got cheaper: the veggie tray, the pie crusts, and the whipped cream.
It's the first rise since {twenty twenty-two|2022}, when the same dinner hit a record {sixty-four dollars|$64.05}.
Farmers blame diesel, labor, and the cost of getting food from the farm to your table. More on the channel.
